title: A novel beta-TrCP1/NRF2 interaction inhibitor for effective anti-inflammatory therapy.
authors: Garcia-Yague, Angel J; Canizares-Moscato, Lucia; Encinar, Jose Antonio; Cazalla, Eduardo; Fernandez-Gines, Raquel; Escoll, Maribel; Rojo, Ana I; Cuadrado, Antonio
one_liner_zh: 该文研究小分子P10抑制beta-TrCP1/NRF2蛋白互作以激活NRF2抗炎，虽涉及蛋白-蛋白互作和分子对接/MD模拟，但对象为蛋白-蛋白而非蛋白-DNA互作，且无TF-DNA结合建模，仅方法部分可借鉴。
abstract: BACKGROUND: Non-communicable chronic diseases are characterized by low-grade inflammation and oxidative stress. Extensive research has identified the transcription factor NRF2 as a potential therapeutic target. Current NRF2 activators, designed to inhibit its repressor KEAP1, often exhibit undesirable side effects. As an alternative approach, we previously developed PHAR, a protein-protein interaction inhibitor of beta-TrCP1/NRF2, which promotes NRF2 activation. Using the same in silico screening platform, we have now identified a novel compound, P10. This small molecule selectively interferes with the beta-TrCP1/NRF2 interaction, leading to NRF2 stabilization and transcriptional activation of its target genes in a beta-TrCP1-dependent manner, demonstrating promising effects in a liver model of acute inflammation. METHODS: After an in silico screening of  approximately 1 million compounds, including molecular docking analysis, ADMET evaluation, and molecular dynamics simulations, we identified and characterized a novel small molecule, P10, which inhibits beta-TrCP1/NRF2 interaction. The compound was validated using luciferase reporter assays, co-immunoprecipitation, and ubiquitination experiments. The specificity of P10 was assessed by comparing NRF2 signatures in wild-type and Nrf2-null cells. The impact of NRF2 activation induced by P10 was investigated by evaluating its antioxidant and anti-inflammatory responses against tert-butyl hydroperoxide and lipopolysaccharide, respectively. Finally, wild-type and Nrf2-null mice were administered P10 intraperitoneally at a dose of 20 mg/kg daily for five consecutive days. Four hours before sacrifice, all animals received a lipopolysaccharide (LPS) injection at 10 mg/kg. RESULTS: P10 selectively disrupts the interaction between beta-TrCP1 and NRF2, thereby inhibiting beta-TrCP1-mediated ubiquitination of NRF2 and leading to the upregulation of NRF2 target genes. Additionally, P10 mitigates oxidative stress induced by tert-butyl hydroperoxide and reduces pro-inflammatory markers in an NRF2-dependent manner in macrophages treated with lipopolysaccharide. In a preclinical model of liver inflammation, P10 specifically targets the liver, significantly attenuating lipopolysaccharide-induced inflammation through the activation of NRF2. This is demonstrated by decreased expression of inflammatory cytokine genes and a reduction in F4/80-stained liver macrophages. Notably, this anti-inflammatory effect is absent in Nrf2-knockout mice, confirming its NRF2-dependent mechanism of action. CONCLUSIONS: P10 emerges as a promising NRF2 activator by selectively disrupting the beta-TrCP1/NRF2 interaction, highlighting its potential as a therapeutic agent for diseases presenting acute liver inflammation.
abstract_zh: 背景：非传染性慢性疾病以低度炎症和氧化应激为特征。大量研究已将转录因子NRF2确定为潜在的治疗靶点。目前旨在抑制其阻遏蛋白KEAP1的NRF2激活剂常表现出不良副作用。作为替代方法，我们先前开发了PHAR，一种针对beta-TrCP1/NRF2相互作用的蛋白质-蛋白质相互作用抑制剂，可促进NRF2激活。利用相同的计算机模拟筛选平台，我们现在鉴定出一种新型化合物P10。该小分子选择性干扰beta-TrCP1/NRF2相互作用，导致NRF2稳定化及其靶基因的转录激活，且以beta-TrCP1依赖性方式发挥作用，在急性炎症的肝脏模型中显示出良好效果。方法：通过对约100万种化合物进行计算机模拟筛选，包括分子对接分析、ADMET评估和分子动力学模拟，我们鉴定并表征了一种新型小分子P10，其抑制beta-TrCP1/NRF2相互作用。该化合物通过荧光素酶报告基因检测、免疫共沉淀和泛素化实验进行验证。P10的特异性通过比较野生型和Nrf2缺失细胞中的NRF2特征进行评估。通过分别评估P10诱导的NRF2激活对叔丁基过氧化氢和脂多糖的抗氧化和抗炎反应，研究了其影响。最后，野生型和Nrf2缺失小鼠以20 mg/kg剂量腹腔注射P10，连续五天。处死前四小时，所有动物接受10 mg/kg脂多糖（LPS）注射。结果：P10选择性破坏beta-TrCP1与NRF2之间的相互作用，从而抑制beta-TrCP1介导的NRF2泛素化，导致NRF2靶基因上调。此外，P10减轻叔丁基过氧化氢诱导的氧化应激，并在脂多糖处理的巨噬细胞中以NRF2依赖性方式降低促炎标志物。在肝脏炎症的临床前模型中，P10特异性靶向肝脏，通过激活NRF2显著减弱脂多糖诱导的炎症。这通过炎症细胞因子基因表达降低和F4/80染色肝脏巨噬细胞减少得以证明。值得注意的是，这种抗炎效应在Nrf2敲除小鼠中缺失，证实了其NRF2依赖性作用机制。结论：P10通过选择性破坏beta-TrCP1/NRF2相互作用，成为一种有前景的NRF2激活剂，突显其作为急性肝脏炎症疾病治疗药物的潜力。
